html:
Ruler of Tenochtitlan and the Aztec Empire from 1502 to 1520, when Hernán Cortés arrived. He was a priest and a seasoned war leader before he was chosen as huey tlatoani, or great speaker.

He pushed the empire to its largest extent, collected tribute from hundreds of towns and tightened the power of the nobility at court. Enemies such as Tlaxcala were never conquered, and they later sided with the Spanish.

In November 1519 he welcomed Cortés into the city, probably to watch and control him. Within days the Spanish took him hostage in his own palace. In June 1520, after Spanish soldiers massacred nobles at a festival at the Templo Mayor, the city rose up. Moctezuma died during the fighting. Spanish accounts say his own people stoned him; some Indigenous accounts say the Spanish killed him.

The story that he took Cortés for the returning god Quetzalcoatl was probably told only after the conquest. A year later came the fall of Tenochtitlan.
